rows.grounds: union or absorption; vā as alternative particle

items.question: In what threefold manner is extinction characterized for the liberated?
premises: Extinction is described as threefold.
Union is included as an alternative mode.
The characterization applies to all without exception.
items.inference: Extinction for the liberated encompasses a threefold mode including union.
items.plain_english: Indeed, extinction is thus threefold, including union, and it is all-encompassing.

items.question: What state shines forth unceasingly and fully for the liberated alone?
premises: The condition belongs to the liberated alone.
It is always full and expansive.
It shines forth without interruption.
items.inference: A full and unceasing radiance belongs exclusively to the liberated.
items.plain_english: O beloved, for the liberated alone, a full radiance always shines forth unceasingly.

items.question: Who is identified as the supreme mother granting all desired ends?
premises: She is the supreme mother.
She is emphatically that very one.
She grants all desired ends.
items.inference: The supreme mother is the sole bestower of all desired ends.
items.plain_english: And she indeed is the supreme Mother, the grantor of all desires.

rows.grounds: vocative address to the goddess of kula

items.question: What identity is asserted between liberation knowledge and kula knowledge?
premises: Liberation knowledge is named.
Kula knowledge is named.
No other knowledge exists apart from these.
items.inference: Liberation knowledge and kula knowledge are identical and exclusive.
items.plain_english: O Lady of Kula, the knowledge of liberation is the knowledge of Kula; there is no other knowledge.

items.question: In which realms do beings attain liberation according to this claim?
premises: Heaven, earth, and the netherworld are named.
Whoever becomes liberated is included.
Liberation occurs in all these realms.
items.inference: Liberation is attainable in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld.
items.plain_english: Indeed, whoever becomes liberated does so in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld.

items.question: What means involving the five elements is declared to grant liberation?
premises: A means is to be known.
It involves the five elements.
It is characterized as giving liberation.
items.inference: The means involving the five elements should be known as granting liberation.
items.plain_english: Likewise, the means should be known as that which, through the five elements, grants liberation.

items.question: From what source does initiation of the nature of kula arise?
premises: Initiation is of the nature of kula.
It comes from the venerable guru.
It issues from the guru's lotus-like mouth.
items.inference: Kula initiation arises from the mouth of the venerable guru.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, initiation consisting of Kula comes from the lotus-like mouth of the venerable Guru.

items.question: How should the wise person engage with kula knowledge after understanding it?
premises: Kula knowledge is to be understood.
Effort is required in engagement.
The wise person should practice it.
items.inference: The wise person should diligently practice kula knowledge after understanding it.
items.plain_english: Having thus understood, the wise person should practice Kula knowledge with effort.

rows.grounds: and not in any other way

items.question: By what means alone can the cause of liberation be truly known?
premises: The cause of liberation is to be known.
It must be known by oneself.
It cannot be known otherwise.
items.inference: The cause of liberation can only be known directly by oneself.
items.plain_english: And the cause of that liberation must be known by oneself, and not otherwise.

rows.grounds: origin in the self; also a name of Brahma

items.question: Why must this teaching be kept secret by divine command?
premises: It is compared to the self-born origin.
It must be kept secret.
The secrecy is enjoined by command.
items.inference: This teaching must be guarded in secrecy by command, like the self-born origin.
uncertainties: The exact referent of ātma+yoniḥ in this context is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, as with the self-born, so this must be kept secret by my command.

items.question: What direct revelation does the goddess demand from the lord without concealment?
premises: The goddess asks who that one is.
She requests a direct answer.
She forbids deceit or concealment.
items.inference: The goddess demands an open revelation of the identity in question.
items.plain_english: Who is she? Speak, O Lord of the world; do not practice deceit, O Lord.

items.question: How does Śaṅkara respond upon hearing Girijā's demand for revelation?
premises: Śaṅkara hears Girijā's words.
He laughs before responding.
He then speaks.
items.inference: Śaṅkara responds to Girijā's demand with laughter and speech.
items.plain_english: Having heard this speech of Girijā, Śaṅkara laughed and spoke.

items.question: What essential nature is attributed to the goddess Kālika as mother?
premises: The goddess is identified as Kālika.
She is called mother.
She embodies all knowledge.
items.inference: Kālika the mother is the embodiment of all knowledge.
items.plain_english: She who is the goddess Kālika, the Mother, is the embodiment of all knowledge.

items.question: How is Kālika's identity as Brahman related to differing philosophical views?
premises: Kālika is identified as Brahman.
This identity is to be known.
Philosophical views exist for the sake of naming.
items.inference: Kālika is Brahman, while differing philosophical views serve only as designations.
items.plain_english: Know that she indeed is Brahman; the various philosophical views exist only for the sake of naming.

items.question: What is the origin of the entire moving and unmoving world?
premises: All this world arises from her.
The world includes moving and unmoving beings.
Her role as source is affirmed.
items.inference: The entire moving and unmoving world is born from her.
items.plain_english: Indeed, from her is born all this world, both moving and unmoving.

rows.grounds: whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss

items.question: What three levels and essential nature characterize the goddess?
premises: The goddess is gross, subtle, and supreme.
She is a single goddess.
Her nature is being, consciousness, and bliss.
items.inference: The goddess manifests as gross, subtle, and supreme, with the nature of being, consciousness, and bliss.
items.plain_english: The Goddess is gross, subtle, and supreme, whose form is being, consciousness, and bliss.

items.question: What sustaining and liberating qualities define the goddess's nature?
premises: She consists of liberation.
She sustains the world.
She is always full of bliss.
items.inference: The goddess is the blissful sustainer of the world and the essence of liberation.
items.plain_english: She consists of liberation, sustains the world, and is likewise always full of bliss.

rows.grounds: at the end of a ritual action

items.question: What ritual analogy explains how results are accomplished at completion?
premises: A ritual reaches completion.
The sacrificial fee is given at completion.
The fee grants accomplishment of the fruit.
items.inference: Just as the sacrificial fee completes a ritual and grants its fruit, so does the goddess complete and fulfill.
items.plain_english: Just as, at the completion of a ritual, the sacrificial fee grants the accomplishment of the fruit.

items.question: Why is the goddess given the name Dakṣiṇā Kālī?
premises: The sacrificial fee grants fulfillment at completion.
This analogy is applied to the goddess.
She is therefore called Dakṣiṇā Kālī.
items.inference: The goddess is called Dakṣiṇā Kālī because she grants the fulfillment of results.
items.plain_english: Therefore, O fair-complexioned one, she is indeed called Dakṣiṇā Kālī.

items.question: What authoritative status does this tantra claim over all other tantras?
premises: All tantras have been spoken.
This tantra encompasses them.
This is stated with certainty.
items.inference: This tantra decisively contains or determines what is taught in all tantras.
items.plain_english: All tantras are spoken with certainty by this tantra.

items.question: What acts of engagement with this tantra are prescribed for devotees?
premises: One may read or recite it to others.
One may hear it.
One may worship it.
items.inference: Reading, reciting, hearing, or worshiping this tantra are prescribed acts of engagement.
items.plain_english: If one reads it, recites it to others, hears it, or worships it.

items.question: What transformative power is attributed to this supreme tantra by analogy?
premises: The touchstone transforms what it contacts.
This tantra is compared to the touchstone.
This tantra is supreme.
items.inference: This supreme tantra has a transformative power like that of the touchstone.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, just as the touchstone transforms, so is this the supreme tantra.

items.question: What analogy illustrates the comprehensive richness contained within this teaching?
premises: All jewels are found in the ocean.
This is stated with certainty.
The analogy implies comprehensive richness.
items.inference: This teaching contains all treasures, just as the ocean contains all jewels.
items.plain_english: Just as all jewels are certainly found in the ocean.

rows.grounds: the dwelling place of all gods

items.question: What analogy affirms this teaching as the established abode of all divine powers?
premises: Mount Meru is the abode of all gods.
This is an established fact.
The same is affirmed again for this teaching.
items.inference: This teaching is established as the abode of all divine powers, like Mount Meru.
items.plain_english: Just as Mount Meru is established as the abode of all gods, so again is this.
